steps.intent: Brazil aims to renew the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism to ensure continued life-saving aid while respecting Syria's sovereignty and emphasizing cross-line deliveries. The main difficulty is Russia's insistence on a shorter six-month extension and stronger language on cross-line aid; we have proposed six months and balanced language to avoid a veto while maintaining humanitarian access.
steps.text:
The Security Council,

Recalling all its previous relevant resolutions and statements of its President concerning the Syrian Arab Republic, in particular resolutions 2139 (2014), 2165 (2014), 2258 (2015), 2332 (2016), 2393 (2017), 2449 (2018), 2504 (2020), 2533 (2020), 2585 (2021), 2642 (2022) and 2672 (2023),

Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, and to the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations,

Reaffirming also the principle of non-intervention and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States,

Expressing grave concern at the dire humanitarian situation in Syria, exacerbated by the earthquake of 6 February 2023 and the ongoing economic crisis, and noting the immense needs of the Syrian people across the country,

Noting the report of the Secretary-General of 10 June 2023 on the humanitarian needs in Syria and his recommendation to extend the cross-border mechanism,

Reaffirming that the cross-border mechanism is temporary and emergency in nature, and that the primary modality for humanitarian assistance should be cross-line deliveries, while recognizing the critical role of cross-border operations in reaching people in need,

Stressing the need for all parties to respect international humanitarian law and humanitarian principles, and to ensure safe, rapid and unhindered access for humanitarian personnel and assistance to all persons in need, including through cross-line and cross-border routes,

Welcoming the work of the United Nations humanitarian agencies and partners in delivering life-saving assistance to the Syrian people, and stressing that humanitarian assistance should be provided in accordance with the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence,

Acting under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations,

1. Decides to renew until 10 January 2024 the authorization for the United Nations humanitarian agencies and partners to use the Bab al-Hawa border crossing for the delivery of humanitarian assistance, as set out in paragraphs 2 and 3 of resolution 2165 (2014) and renewed by subsequent resolutions;

2. Requests the Secretary-General to provide a report to the Security Council on the humanitarian situation in Syria, including cross-line and cross-border operations, no later than 10 December 2023;

3. Reaffirms that the cross-border mechanism is temporary and emergency in nature, and calls for increased cross-line deliveries and humanitarian access through all modalities, and encourages the United Nations to enhance cross-line operations, including through the Bab al-Hawa crossing and other available routes;

4. Reaffirms the need for all parties to respect international humanitarian law and humanitarian principles, and to facilitate safe, rapid and unhindered access for humanitarian personnel and assistance to all persons in need, including through cross-line and cross-border routes, and to ensure the safety and security of humanitarian personnel;

5. Decides to remain actively seized of the matter.

messages.Albania: Albania thanks Brazil and Switzerland for the draft and supports renewing the Bab al-Hawa authorization. We ask the penholders to extend the mandate to 12 months, until 10 July 2024, to allow predictable humanitarian planning, and to rebalance PP6 so that cross-border and cross-line modalities are treated as complementary rather than subordinating cross-border aid to cross-line deliveries. We can support the text with these changes.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of the cross-border mechanism for six months, but the current text must better reflect Syrian sovereignty and Government ownership and the temporary nature of cross-border relief. We ask the penholders to add explicit reference to the Syrian Government's primary responsibility, a clear transition to cross-line delivery as the main channel with a timetable, and the negative impact of unilateral coercive measures. These elements are essential for China's support.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports the renewal as a critical humanitarian lifeline and appreciates the penholders’ compromise. To better reflect the Secretary-General’s recommendation and needs on the ground, we ask that OP1 renew for 12 months and retain the Bab al-Salam crossing alongside Bab al-Hawa. We would adjust the reporting date in OP2 accordingly; these are important improvements, but we remain ready to support a compromise.
messages.France: France supports renewing the cross-border mechanism, but the current six-month, single-crossing text falls short of the humanitarian needs. We ask the penholder to extend the authorization to 12 months and include the Bab al-Salam crossing. France will continue to insist that cross-border access be preserved while cross-line deliveries are expanded.
messages.Gabon: Gabon welcomes the balanced draft and supports renewal of the Bab al-Hawa authorization to prevent further humanitarian deterioration. We appreciate the reaffirmation of Syria's sovereignty and the emphasis on cross-line deliveries alongside cross-border operations. We encourage the penholders to maintain this consensus and call on all parties to facilitate safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the humanitarian purpose of this renewal and appreciates the co-penholders' efforts. To ensure predictable and life-saving access, we ask that OP1 extend the authorization for at least nine months, preferably twelve, and retain the Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai crossings alongside Bab al-Hawa. We also suggest aligning the reporting date with the extended mandate and including reporting on all authorized routes.
messages.Japan: Japan supports the draft as a necessary compromise to preserve lifesaving cross-border humanitarian assistance to Syria, particularly in the northwest. We would have preferred a longer and more predictable renewal, but we will not insist on amendments at this stage; we urge all Council members to support the text and call on all parties to ensure safe, rapid and unhindered access through all modalities.
messages.Malta: Malta supports the draft as a necessary renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism, which remains a lifeline for millions of Syrians. We welcome the reaffirmation of humanitarian principles and the call for expanded cross-line deliveries, and we urge all parties to ensure safe, rapid and unhindered access through all modalities. We encourage the Secretary-General's report to include concrete data on cross-line operations and access constraints.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the draft as a balanced and necessary renewal that preserves the humanitarian lifeline for millions of Syrians while reaffirming Syria's sovereignty and the temporary nature of the cross-border mechanism. We appreciate the penholder's efforts to maintain consensus and urge all Council members to support the text without further delay.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation can support a six-month renewal, but the text must reflect the Syrian Government's role and the harmful impact of unilateral sanctions. We request the above changes to ensure the mechanism remains temporary and does not undermine Syria's sovereignty. We expect the penholders to take these concerns on board.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland, as co-sponsor, supports the draft and believes it provides a vital humanitarian lifeline. We ask that the text explicitly cover early-recovery activities and strengthen reporting on monitoring and funding. We also suggest a preambular reference to resolution 2254 to preserve the political horizon. These are constructive refinements, and we remain flexible.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates supports the renewal of the cross-border mechanism and appreciates the penholders' efforts to preserve Council consensus on this vital humanitarian file. We would welcome a longer renewal, if possible, to ensure predictable delivery, and we ask that the text explicitly encourage early recovery projects, including electricity, water, sanitation, health, education and mine action, in full respect of Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity. We also propose that the Secretary-General's reporting include progress on cross-line deliveries, early recovery and electricity provision.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the renewal and thanks Brazil and Switzerland for their work. We ask that OP1 be extended to 10 July 2024: the Secretary-General and humanitarian partners have been clear that a 12-month mandate is needed for operational certainty. We also suggest a technical correction in OP3 so that it refers to enhancing both cross-line and cross-border operations, including through Bab al-Hawa and other available routes.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the objective of renewing the cross-border mechanism, but a six-month, single-crossing text does not meet the scale of need. We need a 12-month renewal and authorization for the Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai crossings; without those elements we cannot support the draft. We can accept the rest of the text, with the reporting deadline adjusted accordingly.

steps.summary: The revised text is a compromise that preserves the cross-border humanitarian lifeline for six months, adds Bab al-Salam, and incorporates sovereignty, early-recovery, and reporting refinements. It rejects divisive sanctions language and a termination timetable to maintain consensus, while not meeting the maximal US or Russian positions. We expect broad support with China and Russia abstaining.

The Security Council,

Recalling all its previous relevant resolutions and statements of its President concerning the Syrian Arab Republic, in particular resolutions 2139 (2014), 2165 (2014), 2258 (2015), 2332 (2016), 2393 (2017), 2449 (2018), 2504 (2020), 2533 (2020), 2585 (2021), 2642 (2022) and 2672 (2023),

Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, and to the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations,

Reaffirming also the principle of non-intervention and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States,

Reaffirming the primary responsibility of the Syrian Government for the provision of humanitarian assistance to its people and the importance of respecting the sovereignty, territorial integrity and ownership of the Syrian Government in the delivery of humanitarian assistance,

Expressing grave concern at the dire humanitarian situation in Syria, exacerbated by the earthquake of 6 February 2023 and the ongoing economic crisis, and noting the immense needs of the Syrian people across the country,

Noting the report of the Secretary-General of 10 June 2023 on the humanitarian needs in Syria and his recommendation to extend the cross-border mechanism,

Reaffirming that the cross-border mechanism is temporary and emergency in nature, and that cross-line and cross-border deliveries are complementary and both are necessary to meet humanitarian needs in the current circumstances, while recognizing the critical role of cross-border operations in reaching people in need,

Stressing the need for all parties to respect international humanitarian law and humanitarian principles, and to ensure safe, rapid and unhindered access for humanitarian personnel and assistance to all persons in need, including through cross-line and cross-border routes,

Welcoming the work of the United Nations humanitarian agencies and partners in delivering life-saving assistance to the Syrian people, and stressing that humanitarian assistance should be provided in accordance with the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence,

Recalling the need for a lasting political solution to the Syrian conflict in line with resolution 2254 (2015), and reaffirming support for the UN-facilitated political process,

Acting under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations,

1. Decides to renew until 10 January 2024 the authorization for the United Nations humanitarian agencies and partners to use the Bab al-Hawa and Bab al-Salam border crossings for the delivery of humanitarian assistance, including life-saving and early-recovery activities in accordance with humanitarian principles, as set out in paragraphs 2 and 3 of resolution 2165 (2014) and renewed by subsequent resolutions;

2. Requests the Secretary-General to provide a report to the Security Council on the humanitarian situation in Syria, including cross-line and cross-border operations, implementation of the monitoring mechanism, the impact of funding shortfalls, and progress in increasing cross-line deliveries and early recovery projects, no later than 10 December 2023;

4. Reaffirms the need for all parties to respect international humanitarian law and humanitarian principles, and to facilitate safe, rapid and unhindered access for humanitarian personnel and assistance to all persons in need, including through cross-line and cross-border routes, and to ensure the safety and security of humanitarian personnel;

5. Decides to remain actively seized of the matter.

messages.Albania: Albania welcomes the rebalanced PP6 and thanks the penholders for their efforts. We continue to believe that a 12-month renewal is essential for predictable humanitarian planning and for meeting the scale of needs in Syria. We therefore ask that OP1 extend the authorization until 10 July 2024; if consensus requires a six-month renewal, we will not block this humanitarian text.
messages.China: China appreciates the penholder’s partial acceptance of our sovereignty and primary responsibility language. To support the text, we still need OP3 to set a clear trajectory toward cross-line delivery as the main channel and eventual termination of the cross-border mechanism, and a new operative paragraph calling for lifting unilateral coercive measures that impede humanitarian assistance. We also suggest a minor OP2 addition on consultation with the Syrian Government and reporting on unilateral coercive measures. China remains constructive and does not wish to block the renewal.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador welcomes the inclusion of the Bab al-Salam crossing and the balanced language on cross-line and cross-border operations. While we would have preferred a longer renewal for predictable planning, we can support the six-month extension to ensure continuity of life-saving humanitarian assistance. We encourage the Council to adopt the text without delay and to ensure its full implementation and monitoring.
messages.France: France supports the current text. We welcome the inclusion of the Bab al-Salam crossing, which is essential to reach people in need, and we regret that a longer renewal could not be agreed. France will vote in favour and calls for the full, safe and unhindered implementation of the mechanism, while remaining committed to a 12-month renewal and to the political process under resolution 2254 (2015).
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the revised draft as it stands. It preserves the humanitarian cross-border mechanism, reaffirms Syrian sovereignty and the centrality of humanitarian principles, and reflects the balance needed for Council unity. We encourage all members to support the text.
messages.Ghana: Ghana appreciates the inclusion of Bab al-Salam and the alignment of the reporting date, and remains committed to supporting a humanitarian renewal. We still believe a nine-month renewal is the minimum needed for predictable planning, and that Al-Rai should be expressly authorized alongside the other crossings. We ask the penholder to reflect these points in the text; preserving cross-border assistance remains our paramount concern.
messages.Japan: Japan supports the current text, which preserves the cross-border lifeline while reaffirming Syria's sovereignty and the temporary, emergency nature of the mechanism. We urge all members to adopt it without delay so humanitarian agencies can continue life-saving and early-recovery assistance through Bab al-Hawa and Bab al-Salam. Japan emphasizes the need for safe, rapid and unhindered access through all modalities in line with humanitarian principles, and for continued progress on the UN-facilitated political process under resolution 2254.
messages.Malta: Malta supports the current draft and has no further amendments. The renewal of the Bab al-Hawa and Bab al-Salam crossings, together with strengthened reporting on monitoring and access, is essential to respond to the dire humanitarian needs in Syria. We urge the Council to adopt the text without delay and to ensure safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access through all modalities.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the current text as a balanced renewal of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism that preserves Syria's sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity while responding to urgent humanitarian needs. We welcome the reaffirmation that cross-border operations are temporary and emergency in nature and complementary to cross-line deliveries, and we encourage the Secretary-General's reporting to track implementation and progress on cross-line access and early recovery. Mozambique sees no need for further amendments at this stage.
messages.Russian Federation: The current text still crosses Russia's red lines. We cannot accept the inclusion of Bab al-Salam or any cross-border authorization without the Syrian Government's consent and coordination, as this encroaches on Syria's sovereignty. We also insist on language calling for the lifting of unilateral coercive measures, which are a main obstacle to humanitarian access. Unless these changes are made, Russia will not support the draft.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland supports the current revision, which reflects our previous requests on early recovery, monitoring and funding reporting, and resolution 2254. As co-penholder with Brazil, we call on all Council members to support the text and ensure its swift adoption so that life-saving humanitarian access can continue.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE supports the current draft and thanks the penholders for incorporating early-recovery and electricity language in OP3. We continue to believe a longer renewal would provide better humanitarian planning predictability, but we will not block the six-month compromise. To align OP2 with the agreed emphasis on electricity, please add explicit electricity reporting to the Secretary-General's report.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK welcomes the revision to OP3, which now reflects that both cross-line and cross-border operations are necessary. However, we remain convinced that a 12-month renewal is needed to give UN agencies and partners the operational certainty to plan through winter; we therefore ask that OP1 run until 10 July 2024. We will continue to work constructively to ensure the mandate is renewed and does not lapse.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the revised draft and will vote in favour. We appreciate the inclusion of Bab al-Salam and the adjusted reporting requirements. We remain disappointed that Al-Rai is not included and that the authorization is limited to six months, but we will not block this life-saving compromise.

steps.summary: Brazil revised the text to secure Russian acquiescence by limiting the authorization to Bab al-Hawa, while retaining the six-month renewal, adding a weak UCM concern, and accepting technical reporting on electricity. The compromise should avoid a P5 veto and is expected to pass with broad support, with possible abstentions from France and Russia.
steps.text:
The Security Council,

Recalling all its previous relevant resolutions and statements of its President concerning the Syrian Arab Republic, in particular resolutions 2139 (2014), 2165 (2014), 2258 (2015), 2332 (2016), 2393 (2017), 2449 (2018), 2504 (2020), 2533 (2020), 2585 (2021), 2642 (2022) and 2672 (2023),

Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, and to the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations,

Reaffirming also the principle of non-intervention and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States,

Reaffirming the primary responsibility of the Syrian Government for the provision of humanitarian assistance to its people and the importance of respecting the sovereignty, territorial integrity and ownership of the Syrian Government in the delivery of humanitarian assistance,

Expressing grave concern at the dire humanitarian situation in Syria, exacerbated by the earthquake of 6 February 2023 and the ongoing economic crisis, and noting the immense needs of the Syrian people across the country,

Noting the report of the Secretary-General of 10 June 2023 on the humanitarian needs in Syria and his recommendation to extend the cross-border mechanism,

Reaffirming that the cross-border mechanism is temporary and emergency in nature, and that cross-line and cross-border deliveries are complementary and both are necessary to meet humanitarian needs in the current circumstances, while recognizing the critical role of cross-border operations in reaching people in need,

Welcoming the work of the United Nations humanitarian agencies and partners in delivering life-saving assistance to the Syrian people, and stressing that humanitarian assistance should be provided in accordance with the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence,

Recalling the need for a lasting political solution to the Syrian conflict in line with resolution 2254 (2015), and reaffirming support for the UN-facilitated political process,

Acting under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations,

1. Decides to renew until 10 January 2024 the authorization for the United Nations humanitarian agencies and partners to use the Bab al-Hawa border crossing for the delivery of humanitarian assistance, including life-saving and early-recovery activities in accordance with humanitarian principles, as set out in paragraphs 2 and 3 of resolution 2165 (2014) and renewed by subsequent resolutions, in close coordination with the Syrian Government and relevant United Nations humanitarian agencies, and in full respect of the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic;

reasons.Albania: Albania’s record strongly supports maintaining cross-border humanitarian access, and its “support with changes” position would not lead it to block a lifesaving renewal despite the rejected 12-month request.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil is a co-penholder and has consistently supported humanitarian renewals for Syria that preserve life-saving access while reaffirming sovereignty and humanitarian principles. The draft reflects Brazil’s balanced approach and is consistent with its previous votes in favour on this file.
reasons.China: China’s key requests on a clear timetable and stronger language on unilateral coercive measures were only partially accepted. Consistent with its emphasis on Syrian sovereignty and its past practice, China abstains rather than vetoes a humanitarian renewal.
reasons.Ecuador: Ecuador has consistently supported humanitarian cross-border operations and the Brazil-Switzerland penholdership, so it would vote yes despite concerns about sovereignty and the need for cross-line delivery. A pre-vote statement allows it to reaffirm humanitarian principles and call for Council unity.
reasons.France: France supports the draft because it renews the vital Bab al-Hawa mechanism and matches France’s stated policy of avoiding a humanitarian gap, despite preferring a longer mandate and a second crossing; this is consistent with its last negotiation position of support. The statement reiterates France’s known conditions on access, political process, and sanctions.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon’s record and last-round position strongly favour humanitarian renewals in Syria, and it sought no changes to this draft. Supporting the renewal is consistent with its emphasis on humanitarian access, sovereignty and a political solution.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana has consistently supported humanitarian cross-border renewals for Syria and voted for prior compromises despite concerns about duration and access. The draft preserves the essential Bab al-Hawa lifeline, so Ghana would vote yes while explaining its unmet requests.
reasons.Japan: Japan strongly supports humanitarian access in Syria and previously backed the cross-border mechanism, while balancing sovereignty and UN-led political process concerns. It would vote in favour and explain support before the vote.
reasons.Malta: Malta has consistently supported humanitarian cross-border and cross-line access in Syria and voted for previous extensions; this draft reflects its humanitarian priorities, and Malta requested no changes. It would therefore vote in favour and explain its support before the vote.
reasons.Mozambique: Mozambique had already indicated support for the draft and has consistently voted in favour of renewing cross-border humanitarian operations. Its statement stresses humanitarian access while safeguarding sovereignty and political dialogue, consistent with its foreign policy.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia has consistently demanded Syrian Government consent for cross-border aid and stronger action against unilateral sanctions; the penholder did not accept its red-line condition, so it vetoes the draft in line with its established position.
reasons.Switzerland: Switzerland is a co-sponsor of the draft and has consistently supported renewal of the UN cross-border humanitarian mechanism. As a co-penholder, it would vote in favour and would likely make any substantive statement after adoption rather than before the vote.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: The UAE’s last-round position was support with changes, and its requested OP2 language on electricity reporting was accepted. This is consistent with its prior support for renewing the Syria cross-border mechanism while emphasizing humanitarian access, early recovery and Syrian sovereignty.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK supports renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism as essential humanitarian relief, despite its unsuccessful request for a 12-month mandate. Voting in favour is consistent with the UK’s priority on humanitarian access and its prior support for such renewals.
reasons.United States of America: The United States supports the draft as a necessary renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border humanitarian mechanism and had already indicated support in the final negotiation round. The U.S. delegation would likely reserve its explanation of vote for after the vote rather than speak before it.

steps.text:
The Security Council,

Recalling all its previous relevant resolutions and statements of its President concerning the Syrian Arab Republic, in particular resolutions 2139 (2014), 2165 (2014), 2258 (2015), 2332 (2016), 2393 (2017), 2449 (2018), 2504 (2020), 2533 (2020), 2585 (2021), 2642 (2022) and 2672 (2023),

Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, and to the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations,

Reaffirming also the principle of non-intervention and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States,

Reaffirming the primary responsibility of the Syrian Government for the provision of humanitarian assistance to its people and the importance of respecting the sovereignty, territorial integrity and ownership of the Syrian Government in the delivery of humanitarian assistance,

Expressing grave concern at the dire humanitarian situation in Syria, exacerbated by the earthquake of 6 February 2023 and the ongoing economic crisis, and noting the immense needs of the Syrian people across the country,

Noting the report of the Secretary-General of 10 June 2023 on the humanitarian needs in Syria and his recommendation to extend the cross-border mechanism,

Reaffirming that the cross-border mechanism is temporary and emergency in nature, and that cross-line and cross-border deliveries are complementary and both are necessary to meet humanitarian needs in the current circumstances, while recognizing the critical role of cross-border operations in reaching people in need,

Stressing the need for all parties to respect international humanitarian law and humanitarian principles, and to ensure safe, rapid and unhindered access for humanitarian personnel and assistance to all persons in need, including through cross-line and cross-border routes,

Welcoming the work of the United Nations humanitarian agencies and partners in delivering life-saving assistance to the Syrian people, and stressing that humanitarian assistance should be provided in accordance with the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence,

Recalling the need for a lasting political solution to the Syrian conflict in line with resolution 2254 (2015), and reaffirming support for the UN-facilitated political process,

Acting under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations,

1. Decides to renew until 10 January 2024 the authorization for the United Nations humanitarian agencies and partners to use the Bab al-Hawa border crossing for the delivery of humanitarian assistance, including life-saving and early-recovery activities in accordance with humanitarian principles, as set out in paragraphs 2 and 3 of resolution 2165 (2014) and renewed by subsequent resolutions, in close coordination with the Syrian Government and relevant United Nations humanitarian agencies, and in full respect of the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic;

2. Requests the Secretary-General to provide a report to the Security Council on the humanitarian situation in Syria, including cross-line and cross-border operations, implementation of the monitoring mechanism, the impact of funding shortfalls, and progress in increasing cross-line deliveries and early recovery projects, including the provision of electricity, no later than 10 December 2023;

3. Reaffirms that the cross-border mechanism is temporary and emergency in nature, calls for increased cross-line deliveries and humanitarian access through all modalities, with a view to making cross-line delivery, over time, the main channel for humanitarian assistance and enabling the eventual termination of the cross-border mechanism once conditions permit and in line with humanitarian needs, and encourages the United Nations to enhance both cross-line and cross-border operations, including through the Bab al-Hawa crossing and other available routes, and to scale up early recovery projects, including the provision of electricity, water, sanitation, health, education and mine action, in full respect of the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria, while ensuring that cross-border operations remain temporary and emergency in nature and do not undermine the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria;

4. Stresses that unilateral coercive measures should not impede the delivery of humanitarian assistance and calls upon all Member States to take appropriate steps to avoid adverse humanitarian consequences of such measures, in accordance with international law;

5. Reaffirms the need for all parties to respect international humanitarian law and humanitarian principles, and to facilitate safe, rapid and unhindered access for humanitarian personnel and assistance to all persons in need, including through cross-line and cross-border routes, and to ensure the safety and security of humanitarian personnel;

6. Decides to remain actively seized of the matter.

before.Albania: Albania will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank Brazil and Switzerland for their efforts to preserve the vital humanitarian lifeline for millions of Syrians. We had sought a 12-month renewal because predictability is essential for humanitarian planning and funding, and we regret that this was not accepted. Nonetheless, we cannot vote against the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism, which remains indispensable. Cross-line deliveries are important, but they cannot replace cross-border assistance under current conditions. We call on all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, to ensure safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access to all people in need and to uphold humanitarian principles.
before.Brazil: I speak on behalf of Brazil and Switzerland as co-penholders of this file. We thank all Council members for their constructive engagement throughout the negotiations. The text before the Council is balanced and pragmatic: it renews the authorization for the Bab al-Hawa crossing until 10 January 2024 in order to sustain life-saving humanitarian assistance to millions of Syrians in need, while reaffirming the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and the humanitarian principles that must guide all relief operations. It also rightly emphasizes the importance of scaling up cross-line deliveries and early recovery projects and recognizes that the cross-border mechanism is temporary and emergency in nature. We further stress that unilateral coercive measures must not impede the delivery of humanitarian assistance. Brazil will vote in favour of the draft resolution and encourages all members to do the same.
before.China: China thanks Brazil and Switzerland for their efforts and for partially incorporating China’s proposals. China has consistently maintained that humanitarian assistance to Syria must respect Syria’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and the ownership of the Syrian Government. Cross-border delivery is a temporary emergency arrangement and must not replace cross-line delivery as the main channel. The draft before us contains some useful elements on cross-line deliveries and unilateral coercive measures, but it still fails to establish a clear timetable for the eventual termination of the cross-border mechanism, does not require reporting in consultation with the Syrian Government, and does not clearly call for the lifting of unilateral coercive measures that exacerbate the humanitarian situation. Given that the draft still falls short of China’s concerns, China will abstain on this draft resolution. We hope the Council will continue to work on the basis of respecting Syria’s sovereignty while addressing the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people.
before.Ecuador: Thank you, Mr. President. Ecuador will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The humanitarian situation in Syria remains dire, aggravated by the February earthquake and the ongoing economic crisis. We support maintaining predictable cross-border humanitarian access through the Bab al-Hawa crossing while respecting Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and we stress that cross-border relief is temporary and emergency in nature and complementary to cross-line deliveries. We thank Brazil and Switzerland for their efforts and call on all Council members to unite around the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this resolution. The renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism is indispensable for millions of Syrians, and the Council must not allow a gap in the delivery of life-saving assistance. France regrets, however, that the Council has again settled for a six-month renewal and that an additional crossing, including Bab al-Salam, has not been authorized; humanitarian needs require a longer, more predictable mandate and the use of all available routes. We call on all parties to ensure safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access in accordance with humanitarian principles. France recalls that any normalization, reconstruction or lifting of sanctions remains conditional on a credible and inclusive political process under resolution 2254 (2015).
before.Gabon: Mr. President, Gabon thanks the penholders for their efforts. Given the severe humanitarian needs in Syria, including those exacerbated by the February earthquake, Gabon supports the renewal of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism as a temporary and emergency measure. We do so while reaffirming respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, and we stress that cross-border and cross-line deliveries must be complementary and carried out in line with humanitarian principles. We also call for scaled-up early recovery and unhindered humanitarian access, and we reiterate the importance of advancing a lasting political solution consistent with resolution 2254 (2015). Gabon will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.Ghana: Ghana thanks the co-penholders for their efforts to preserve the cross-border humanitarian lifeline to millions of Syrians in need. We will vote in favour of this draft because the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa crossing is essential and time-sensitive, especially in the aftermath of the February earthquake and the worsening economic and humanitarian situation. At the same time, we regret that our call for a longer and more predictable renewal, and for the inclusion of all previously authorized crossings, was not fully reflected. We would have preferred a nine-month renewal and broader access through Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai, which would better support humanitarian planning and reach more people in need. We nevertheless support this resolution as a necessary step to prevent the interruption of life-saving assistance, and we urge the Council to continue working toward a more predictable and comprehensive humanitarian arrangement consistent with the humanitarian principles and the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria.
before.Japan: Japan votes in favour of this draft resolution. The humanitarian situation in Syria remains extremely grave, including the consequences of the February earthquake and the ongoing economic crisis, and millions of people depend on cross-border assistance for their survival. Japan supports the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa authorization, while stressing that all humanitarian deliveries must be conducted in full respect of Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and in accordance with humanitarian principles. We also underscore the importance of increasing cross-line deliveries, ensuring safe and unhindered humanitarian access through all modalities, and advancing a lasting political solution in line with resolution 2254 (2015).
before.Malta: Malta thanks Brazil and Switzerland for their efforts to secure a humanitarian extension. The humanitarian situation in Syria remains dire, including after the February earthquake. Malta will vote in favour because renewing the Bab al-Hawa crossing is a lifeline for millions of people in need and must continue while we pursue expanded cross-line access. We stress that humanitarian assistance must be delivered in accordance with the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence, and that the sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity of Syria must be respected. We call on all parties to ensure safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access and to work towards a lasting political solution in line with resolution 2254.
before.Mozambique: Mr. President, Mozambique will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank Brazil and Switzerland for their efforts to preserve a humanitarian lifeline for the Syrian people at a time of grave need. The renewal of the Bab al-Hawa crossing is necessary to ensure that life-saving assistance reaches civilians, particularly in the context of the earthquake and the worsening economic crisis. At the same time, we stress that the cross-border mechanism is temporary and emergency in nature; humanitarian assistance must be delivered in full respect of Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and in accordance with the humanitarian principles. We call on all parties to facilitate safe, rapid and unhindered access, including through cross-line deliveries, and to support the UN-facilitated political process in line with resolution 2254 (2015).
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation has consistently stated that the cross-border mechanism is temporary and emergency in nature and must not undermine the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria. We appreciate the removal of Bab al-Salam from the text and the limited attention given to unilateral coercive measures, but these changes do not meet the fundamental concerns we set out. The draft still fails to make the use of the Bab al-Hawa crossing conditional on close coordination with and the consent of the Syrian Government. It also does not call for the immediate lifting of unilateral coercive measures, which continue to worsen the humanitarian situation and impede early recovery. Humanitarian assistance to Syria must be delivered in full respect of Syrian sovereignty and through strengthened cross-line operations, with the Syrian Government bearing primary responsibility. For these reasons, the Russian Federation cannot support this draft resolution and will vote against it.
before.United Arab Emirates: Thank you, Mr. President. The United Arab Emirates will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The humanitarian situation in Syria remains dire, exacerbated by the February earthquake and a severe economic crisis, and the cross-border mechanism continues to provide a vital lifeline to millions in need. At the same time, we stress that this mechanism must remain temporary and emergency in nature and must be implemented in full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. We welcome the inclusion of electricity in the Secretary-General’s reporting on early-recovery progress, and we call for serious efforts to scale up cross-line deliveries and early-recovery projects, including electricity, water, sanitation and health. We urge all parties to ensure safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access and to protect humanitarian personnel. We also stress that unilateral coercive measures should not impede the delivery of humanitarian assistance. The United Arab Emirates thanks Brazil and Switzerland for their efforts as penholders.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution. We do so because the United Nations cross-border mechanism remains a lifeline for millions of Syrians in need, and it must not be allowed to lapse. We thank Brazil and Switzerland for their efforts. The United Kingdom regrets that the Council has not agreed the twelve-month renewal that the Secretary-General and humanitarian partners have repeatedly said is necessary to provide operational certainty. A six-month renewal leaves humanitarian agencies in a continued cycle of contingency planning. We also underline that cross-border and cross-line deliveries are complementary, and that all parties must ensure safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access in accordance with international humanitarian law. The humanitarian imperative must guide this Council, and the United Kingdom urges all members to support the renewal.

after.Albania: Albania takes the floor after the vote. We thank Brazil and Switzerland for their persistent efforts to preserve the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism, which remains an indispensable lifeline for millions of Syrians in need. Albania voted in favour of the draft resolution because we could not accept allowing humanitarian assistance to be interrupted. We would have preferred a longer and more predictable renewal, but the text before us was a balanced compromise that would have saved lives and allowed humanitarian actors to continue their work, particularly in the aftermath of the February earthquake and the worsening economic crisis in Syria. We deeply regret that the Security Council has once again failed to act, not because the humanitarian needs are lacking, but because a single veto has blocked the renewal of this vital mechanism. This is a grave disappointment for the Syrian people and for all those who rely on the Council to uphold its responsibilities. Cross-border deliveries are not a substitute for cross-line access, but under current conditions they cannot be replaced by cross-line deliveries alone. We call on all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, to ensure safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access to all people in need and to respect international humanitarian law and humanitarian principles. Albania remains committed to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria, and to a lasting political solution in line with resolution 2254 (2015). The Council must not remain paralysed while human lives are at stake.
after.Brazil: Mr. President, I take the floor on behalf of Brazil and Switzerland as co-penholders of this file. We deeply regret that the Security Council has not been able to adopt the draft resolution before us, despite the broad support it received. The text was balanced, pragmatic and the product of extensive consultations. It sought to preserve the Bab al-Hawa humanitarian lifeline for millions of Syrians in need, while reaffirming Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, and while strengthening cross-line deliveries, early recovery and respect for humanitarian principles. We incorporated concerns raised by members, including on the temporary and emergency nature of the cross-border mechanism and on the humanitarian impact of unilateral coercive measures. The absence of a renewal now creates serious uncertainty for humanitarian partners and for the civilians who depend on this assistance for food, medicine, water and shelter. Brazil and Switzerland remain committed to working with all Council members to prevent a gap in life-saving assistance and to ensure that humanitarian access is maintained through all modalities, in full respect for international humanitarian law. We call on all parties to facilitate safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access and to renew their engagement in good faith. The humanitarian needs of the Syrian people must remain above politics. Thank you.
after.France: Mr. President, France deeply regrets that the draft resolution renewing the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism was not adopted owing to the negative vote of the Russian Federation. This is a grave failure for the Security Council at a moment when millions of Syrians depend on cross-border humanitarian assistance. France voted in favour and will continue to defend the full, safe, rapid and unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid to all Syrians in need, in accordance with humanitarian principles. We call on the Russian Federation to shoulder its responsibilities and on all Council members to avoid a humanitarian gap. The cross-border mechanism remains indispensable, and France will remain mobilized with its partners, while recalling that normalization, reconstruction and the lifting of sanctions remain conditional on a credible and inclusive political process under resolution 2254 (2015).
after.Gabon:
Mr. President, Gabon voted in favour of the draft resolution because the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism is a humanitarian necessity for millions of Syrians, particularly in the aftermath of the February earthquake and amid the worsening economic crisis. We deeply regret that this Council has been unable to adopt the text, and we recall that the humanitarian imperative must transcend political divisions.

Gabon reaffirms the importance of respecting Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, and stresses that cross-border assistance is temporary and emergency in nature and must be complementary to cross-line deliveries. The failure to renew the authorization risks interrupting life-saving assistance to the most vulnerable. We urge all Council members and all parties to work urgently to prevent a humanitarian gap, to ensure safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access through all modalities, and to advance a lasting political solution consistent with resolution 2254 (2015). Gabon will remain actively engaged in these efforts.
after.Ghana: Thank you, Mr. President. Ghana voted in favour of this draft because the renewal of the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism is a humanitarian necessity for millions of Syrians, particularly in the aftermath of the February earthquake and amid the worsening economic crisis. We deeply regret that the Council was unable to adopt the resolution today. The humanitarian imperative must not be lost in political divisions. We call on all members to continue constructive engagement so that the cross-border lifeline is not interrupted, and we reiterate our preference for a longer, more predictable renewal and for the use of all available crossings, including Bab al-Salam and Al-Rai, to reach those in need. At the same time, humanitarian assistance must continue to respect Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and be delivered in accordance with humanitarian principles. Ghana urges all parties to facilitate safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access through both cross-border and cross-line routes, and we reaffirm our support for a lasting political solution in line with resolution 2254 (2015). The Security Council must remain actively seized of this matter and act with the urgency that the Syrian people deserve.
after.Malta:
Mr. President,

Malta voted in favour of the draft resolution before the Council, and we deeply regret that it was not adopted. With the previous authorization having expired, the Council’s failure today puts at risk a lifeline on which millions of Syrians depend, especially in the aftermath of the February earthquake and amid a severe economic crisis.

Malta thanks Brazil and Switzerland for their persistent efforts to bridge positions. We reaffirm that humanitarian assistance must be delivered in full accordance with the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence, and with respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. Cross-border operations remain indispensable in the current circumstances, while cross-line deliveries must be expanded and facilitated.

We urge all Council members not to allow humanitarian access to become a casualty of political division. Malta calls on all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, to ensure safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access to all persons in need, and we commit to continuing to work with the penholders and all members to prevent a humanitarian gap and to support a lasting political solution in line with resolution 2254 (2015).
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted against this draft resolution because it failed to reflect the fundamental principles that must guide the Council’s work on Syria: respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, and respect for the primary responsibility of the Syrian Government in providing humanitarian assistance to its people.

We have consistently stated that the cross-border mechanism is temporary and emergency in nature. It cannot be treated as an indefinite substitute for cross-line deliveries or as a means of undermining Syrian sovereignty. The draft before us did not make the use of the Bab al-Hawa crossing conditional on close coordination with and the consent of the Syrian Government. It did not establish a clear timetable for the eventual termination of the cross-border mechanism. It also did not contain the firm demand for the lifting of unilateral coercive measures that is required if we are to speak seriously about improving the humanitarian situation and enabling early recovery. Declaratory language calling on States to avoid the adverse effects of such measures is not enough.

We thank Brazil and Switzerland for their efforts, but the text remained unbalanced and did not meet our principled concerns. The Russian Federation is not opposed to humanitarian assistance to the Syrian people. We support safe and unhindered humanitarian access through cross-line routes, in coordination with the Syrian Government and in accordance with humanitarian principles. We will continue to work with the Syrian Government, United Nations agencies and all interested partners to ensure that genuine humanitarian needs are addressed, and we remain open to constructive dialogue on a formula that respects Syria’s sovereignty and the Council’s responsibilities.
after.Switzerland: Switzerland voted in favour of the draft resolution and deeply regrets that it has not been adopted. As co-penholder with Brazil, we worked for a balanced, pragmatic and humanitarian text that would have preserved a vital lifeline for millions of Syrians in need. The failure to renew the Bab al-Hawa authorization, at a time when humanitarian needs remain enormous after the February earthquake and amid a severe economic crisis, is a grave setback. Switzerland is particularly concerned that the Council has been unable to prevent an interruption of cross-border humanitarian assistance. We call on all members to return to negotiations without delay and in good faith to preserve humanitarian access. All parties must respect international humanitarian law and ensure safe, rapid and unhindered access through all modalities. Cross-border and cross-line deliveries are complementary; increased cross-line operations are necessary, but under current conditions they cannot replace cross-border assistance. Humanitarian assistance must continue to be delivered in accordance with the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence, and in full respect of Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. Switzerland remains committed to supporting a political solution in line with resolution 2254 (2015) and to ensuring that the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people are not held hostage to political divisions.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr. President, the United Kingdom is deeply disappointed that the Security Council has failed to renew the Bab al-Hawa cross-border mechanism. Thirteen members voted in favour of a balanced text that would have preserved a vital humanitarian lifeline for millions of Syrians in need. Russia’s solitary veto has prevented the Council from acting. We regret that deeply. This veto has no humanitarian justification. It will not improve cross-line access; it will make it harder to reach people in need. The United Kingdom rejects any suggestion that life-saving assistance should be made conditional on the consent of the Syrian regime. The humanitarian imperative must prevail. We will continue to work with partners to ensure that United Nations agencies can deliver assistance to the Syrian people, and we call on Russia to reconsider its position. The Council must not abandon the Syrian people.
after.United States of America:
Mr. President, the United States voted in favor of this resolution, and we deeply regret that the Council has failed to adopt it. Renewing the Bab al-Hawa crossing is not a political concession to any party; it is a humanitarian lifeline for millions of Syrians, including those still reeling from the February earthquakes and the worsening economic crisis. The Secretary-General and humanitarian partners have been clear about the needs on the ground and the importance of predictable access.

We thank Brazil and Switzerland for their constructive efforts to preserve cross-border assistance while reaffirming Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity and the need to scale up cross-line deliveries. The United States was prepared to support a longer and more predictable renewal, as the humanitarian community has urged. Instead, a veto has blocked a text that had broad support in this Council and that would have saved lives.

We call on Russia to reconsider its position and allow the Council to extend the cross-border mechanism without further delay. The Syrian people cannot wait. The United States will continue to work with partners to ensure life-saving assistance reaches those in need and to press for safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access through all modalities, in accordance with humanitarian principles and in support of a lasting political solution under resolution 2254.
